questions.answer: I studied business administration at university, with a focus on management. It gave me a broad understanding of how organisations actually run, which has proved surprisingly [[invaluable]] in the work I do now.

questions.q: Why did you choose that subject?
questions.answer: Partly because of my father, to be honest. Growing up around his small business, I saw how much planning goes into keeping things running, and I suppose that [[sparked my interest]] in management quite early on.

questions.q: Did you enjoy your time at university?
questions.answer: Very much, on the whole. The coursework was demanding at times, but I made some lifelong friends and took part in a few debating events. Those years really helped me become more [[self-assured]] and independent.

questions.q: What was the most useful thing you learned?
questions.answer: Probably how to communicate clearly in a professional setting. We did a lot of group presentations, which I dreaded at first, but they gradually made me far more [[articulate]], and I rely on that every day at work.

questions.q: Would you like to study something else in the future?
questions.answer: Yes, I'd love to do a master's abroad, possibly in international education or management. I feel it would deepen my understanding of the field and [[open doors]] that aren't really available to me here.
